learn.title: Understanding the Duck Curve Problem
learn.intro: The duck curve illustrates a major challenge facing solar-rich grids: as solar generation ramps down at sunset, demand spikes simultaneously. This mismatch forces grid operators to rapidly deploy flexible resources, making stable electricity supply increasingly difficult to maintain during peak evening hours.
learn.c1_text: The duck curve shows the gap between total electricity demand and renewable generation throughout the day. As solar output drops after sunset, net demand surges—like a duck’s belly. This steep ramp-up requires fast-response power plants to avoid blackouts, stressing traditional infrastructure.
learn.c2_text: With high solar penetration, midday oversupply can drive prices negative, while evening peaks strain backup systems. Utilities must balance supply and demand in real time. Without sufficient storage or flexible generation, sudden drops in renewables can destabilize frequency and voltage levels.
learn.c3_text: India has over 70 GW of solar capacity installed by 2023. States like Gujarat and Rajasthan experience sharp evening ramps. To manage the duck curve, India is investing heavily in battery storage projects and pumped hydro to store excess daytime solar energy for use during peak demand.

learn.title: Virtual Power Plants Explained
learn.intro: Virtual power plants (VPPs) aggregate thousands of distributed energy resources using AI and software. By coordinating rooftop solar, home batteries, and smart appliances, VPPs act like a single power plant—enhancing grid flexibility and resilience without building new centralized facilities.
learn.c1_text: A VPP connects small-scale energy assets—like home solar panels and electric vehicles—into one virtual system. Think of it as a digital orchestra conductor synchronizing dozens of instruments. AI algorithms predict usage patterns and dispatch stored energy when needed most.
learn.c2_text: AI enables real-time optimization across millions of nodes. Machine learning forecasts weather and consumption trends, automatically shifting loads or discharging batteries to stabilize the grid. This intelligent coordination reduces reliance on fossil-fuel peaker plants and enhances overall efficiency.
learn.c3_text: India launched its first VPP pilot in Delhi in 2022, aggregating rooftop solar and batteries from residential buildings. With over 15 million rooftop solar connections nationwide, VPPs offer immense potential for demand response and peak shaving under India's Smart Grid mission.

learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Long Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries offer a breakthrough in long-duration energy storage, capable of storing power for over 100 hours. Unlike lithium-ion, they rely on abundant iron and oxygen, promising low-cost seasonal storage crucial for deep decarbonization and reliable renewable grids.
learn.c1_text: These batteries use reversible rusting: iron oxidizes during discharge and is restored via electrolysis. Oxygen from air moves through a porous cathode, while iron pellets form the anode. This process stores energy chemically—not electrically—enabling ultra-long durations at minimal cost.
learn.c2_text: Iron is 100x cheaper than lithium and globally available. A 100-hour iron-air system costs about $20/kWh compared to $150/kWh for lithium-ion. This makes multi-day storage economically viable for utilities needing seasonal backup during prolonged cloudy or calm periods.
learn.c3_text: India aims to deploy 500 GWh of storage by 2030 under its National Storage Roadmap. Startups like Aeson Nanoflow are developing iron-based prototypes. These could complement India’s 500 GW non-fossil target by providing affordable long-duration storage for rural microgrids.

learn.title: How Solar Panels Generate Electricity
learn.intro: Solar photovoltaic (PV) panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect. When photons strike semiconductor materials, they knock electrons loose, generating direct current. This clean, silent technology powers homes and industries worldwide.
learn.c1_text: When sunlight hits a solar cell, photons transfer energy to electrons in the semiconductor layer (usually silicon). This knocks them loose, creating electron-hole pairs. Metal contacts on the cell capture these flowing electrons, producing DC electricity that flows through circuits.
learn.c2_title: 🔌 From DC to Usable AC Power
learn.c2_text: Solar panels produce direct current (DC), but homes run on alternating current (AC). An inverter converts DC to AC, synchronizing phase and frequency with the grid. Modern inverters also monitor performance and shut down safely during outages to protect workers.
learn.c3_text: Under Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, India allocated $2.6 billion to boost domestic solar manufacturing. Over 20 GW of solar capacity was added in 2023 alone. The government plans to reach 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030, with solar contributing over 280 GW.

learn.title: Green Steel Through Hydrogen Reduction
learn.intro: Green steel replaces coal with hydrogen in steelmaking, eliminating carbon emissions. Using hydrogen-based direct reduction, this method produces only water vapor as waste. As steel accounts for 8% of global CO2 emissions, green steel is vital for decarbonizing heavy industry.
learn.c1_text: Conventional blast furnaces burn coal to extract iron ore, releasing CO2. Green steel uses hydrogen instead—reacting with iron ore to produce molten iron and water vapor. This process cuts emissions by up to 95%, revolutionizing one of the world’s most carbon-intensive industries.
learn.c2_text: Green hydrogen comes from splitting water using renewable electricity. Producing 1 ton of steel requires ~50 kg of hydrogen. For large-scale adoption, hydrogen must be produced cost-effectively (~$1.50/kg) and transported safely. Infrastructure investments are key to scaling this technology.
learn.c3_text: India produced 118 million tons of crude steel in FY2023. Under its National Green Hydrogen Mission, India plans to become a global hub for green hydrogen production. Major steelmakers like Tata Steel are piloting hydrogen-based furnaces to align with India's net-zero 2070 commitment.

learn.title: Smart Grids and Digital Metering
learn.intro: Smart grids modernize electrical networks with digital communication, automation, and real-time monitoring. Advanced metering infrastructure tracks usage instantly, enabling dynamic pricing and efficient load management. These innovations are essential for integrating variable renewables and empowering consumers.
learn.c1_text: Smart grids use sensors, IoT devices, and two-way communication to monitor voltage, current, and frequency across the network. This allows instant detection of faults and automatic rerouting of power. Utilities gain unprecedented visibility into grid health, improving reliability and reducing outage durations significantly.
learn.c2_text: Advanced meters record hourly consumption data, supporting time-of-use tariffs. Consumers shift usage to off-peak hours when rates drop. During high demand, utilities send signals to reduce load, avoiding blackouts. This balance between supply and demand stabilizes prices and defers costly infrastructure upgrades.
learn.c3_text: India launched the Smart Meter National Grid project to install 250 million smart meters by 2025. Over 75 million have been deployed so far. States like Uttar Pradesh and Delhi lead adoption. This supports India’s goal of 500 GW renewable capacity and improves billing accuracy for distribution companies.
